patients.summary: Uninsured construction laborer and groundskeeper with severe alcohol use disorder, untreated chronic hepatitis C, alcoholic cirrhosis and asplenia after a 2013 splenectomy, who joins in 2018. Over the years he develops porphyria cutanea tarda, folate deficiency anemia, vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism and severe malnutrition, and in July 2026 is hospitalized with alcoholic pancreatitis complicated by withdrawal delirium and ARDS.

orders.reason: Chronic hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, high MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
42 y/o man here to set up care. Hasn't had a regular doctor in years. Coworker on a job site recommended us.

HPI: Feels okay overall. Came in mostly because his wife pushed him to, and because he knows he has hep C and has never done anything about it. He was told he had it around the time of his accident in 2013, never followed up. No records available, he doesn't remember where the testing was done.
Drinks every day. Mostly vodka, he estimates close to a bottle a day, beer on weekends on top of that. Has been at this level for well over a decade, started heavy drinking in his mid-20s. No withdrawal seizures that he knows of. Morning shakes some days, settles with a drink. Not interested in treatment today, but willing to talk about it.
Splenectomy 2013 after a car accident (he was the passenger). Was told afterward he should have shots and 'carry antibiotics' and did neither.
No abdominal swelling, no vomiting blood, no black stools, no confusion per his account.

PMH: hep C (untreated), splenectomy 2013.
Meds: none.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father drank heavily and died of liver cirrhosis. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Nobody with blood cancers or porphyria that he knows.
SH: married. Construction laborer, also mows and does groundskeeping part time in the summer. Never smoked. No drugs. No health insurance.

Exam: thin, alert, smells of alcohol, cooperative. No jaundice. No spider angiomata seen. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed midline scar, liver edge not clearly felt, no fluid wave. No asterixis. Mild fine tremor of outstretched hands. Skin without rash.

A/P:
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe. AUDIT-C 11. Discussed liver risk plainly, he listened. Not ready for detox or a program. Start thiamine 100 mg daily. Will keep raising it.
2. Chronic hepatitis C, reported. Checking antibody and viral load, HBV serologies, HIV. Liver panel, INR, CBC, GGT. Abdominal ultrasound to look at the liver.
3. Asplenia after splenectomy. Penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily for prophylaxis. Starting his vaccines today: PCV13, Hib, MenACWY and MenB first doses, plus Tdap since he can't recall the last one. Polysaccharide pneumococcal in 8 weeks. Told him any fever over 101 means a call to us the same day.
4. Uninsured: front desk to give him the cash price sheet for labs and imaging.

RTC 6 weeks after ultrasound.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCV13 L deltoid, Hib R deltoid, MenACWY L deltoid, MenB R deltoid, Tdap L deltoid (separate sites marked). VIS sheets given. Lot numbers in the immunization record. Tolerated, waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with results. Hep C antibody reactive and viral load positive at about 1.2 million, so this is active chronic hep C. HBV surface antigen and antibody both negative, so not immune to hep B and will vaccinate. HIV negative. AST higher than ALT, GGT high, platelets a bit low, INR 1.1. Explained these fit liver injury from alcohol plus the virus. Ultrasound is booked for the 24th. He asked what it costs, gave him the front desk number.

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound, complete abdomen.
HISTORY: Chronic hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Liver: normal size, nodular surface contour with coarse heterogeneous echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion. Main portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Hepatic veins patent.
Gallbladder: no stones, no wall thickening. No pericholecystic fluid.
Bile ducts: common bile duct 4 mm, not dilated.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Spleen: surgically absent.
Kidneys: right 10.9 cm, left 11.2 cm, normal echogenicity, no hydronephrosis, no stones.
Aorta: normal caliber.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Nodular, coarsened liver consistent with cirrhosis. No focal liver lesion. No ascites. Patent portal vein. Post-splenectomy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back to go over the ultrasound. Still drinking daily, maybe a little less he says. Has taken the thiamine most days. Penicillin: honest that he took it for about a week and stopped, says he forgets the second dose and doesn't see the point when he feels fine.
No abdominal swelling, no leg swelling, no bleeding, no confusion.

O: BP and pulse as charted. Thin. No jaundice, no ascites on exam, no asterixis.

Ultrasound 4/24: nodular coarse liver c/w cirrhosis, no mass, no ascites, portal vein open. Labs from April reviewed with him again.

A/P:
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis, compensated. Added to problem list. Hep C a second driver. Spent a good part of the visit on what cirrhosis means and why stopping drinking is the single biggest thing. He said he'd think about it.
2. Chronic hep C, confirmed with viral load.
3. Asplenia. Back over why the penicillin matters. MenB #2, hep A #1, hep B #1 today. Nurse visit in 3-4 weeks for the polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine, MenACWY #2, hep B #2.
4. AUD, severe. Continue thiamine.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work, still in work boots. PPSV23 L deltoid, MenACWY #2 R deltoid, hep B #2 L deltoid. No reaction to April or May shots per pt besides a sore arm. Next due: hep A #2 and hep B #3 in November. Reminder card given.

documents.title: Fill History
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pulled outside fill history while prepping for August visit. Thiamine filled 4/10 and 6/12. Penicillin VK filled once, 4/10, 30-day supply, not refilled. Flagged for PCP.

documents.title: Missed Visit Outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re: missed appt yesterday. Pt says a job ran late, apologized. Rebooked for late October, asked for an early slot. Reminded him of the thiamine refill on file.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Rescheduled after August no-show. Busy season over. Drinking unchanged, 'still a bottle most days.' Takes thiamine when he remembers. Penicillin not taking; we talked about it again and he agreed to try to keep the bottle by the coffee maker. No fevers this year. No swelling, no bleeding, no confusion.
O: vitals as charted, weight stable. No jaundice, no ascites, no asterixis. Fine tremor.
A/P:
- Cirrhosis, compensated: CMP, CBC, INR today.
- AUD severe: AUDIT-C 11. Offered referral to an outpatient program, declined for now. Continue thiamine.
- Asplenia: penicillin re-sent. Flu shot today. Hep A #2 and hep B #3 due in late November, nurse visit booked.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver numbers about the same as April. Platelets still mildly low, INR stable. No change in plan. Pt notified by phone, voicemail.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep A #2 R deltoid and hep B #3 L deltoid. Hep A and hep B series now complete. Tolerated well. Asked whether he has been taking the penicillin, he shrugged and said 'some days.' Passed along to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Winter is slow at work so he's had more time on his hands and admits drinking has crept up. Wife is frustrated with him. No jaundice he's noticed, no belly swelling, eating 'one real meal a day.' Thiamine yes, penicillin mostly no.
O: vitals as charted. Thin, no jaundice, no ascites, no asterixis.
A/P:
1. AUD severe, AUDIT-C 12. Long talk. Gave him the number for the regional recovery line and a list of meetings in town. He took the paper.
2. Compensated cirrhosis: labs today.
3. Asplenia: same counseling on penicillin and fever.
4. Eat more regularly, protein with each meal.
RTC 6 months for physical, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gregory, your labs look about like last fall. Liver tests are still elevated in the pattern we see with alcohol, and your platelets are a little low, which fits the cirrhosis. Blood counts otherwise okay, kidneys normal. Nothing urgent. The most helpful thing for these numbers is cutting back on drinking. See you in September.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called for thiamine refill, ran out a couple weeks ago. Sent 90-day supply per standing order. Asked about penicillin, he declined a refill, says he has 'plenty left.'

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM
Working full days, groundskeeping on weekends through the fall. Drinking the same. Mood okay, PHQ-2 1. Sleeps poorly some nights. Thiamine most days. Penicillin: not taking.
ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no abdominal swelling, no blood in stool, no dark stool, no vomiting blood, no fevers.
Exam: thin but steady. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, scar healed, no ascites, liver edge not felt today. No edema. Skin: sun-tanned forearms, no rash. Neuro: fine postural tremor, gait normal.
Health maintenance: vaccines for asplenia and hep A/B complete; MenACWY booster due 2023. Tdap 2018. Flu shot today. Colon screening starts at 45, not yet. HIV screen done 2018.
A/P: compensated alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hep C, asplenia, severe AUD. Labs today. Same message on alcohol; he isn't ready. RTC 5-6 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from the physical: liver enzymes in his usual range, platelets mildly low, INR 1.2, kidneys and electrolytes normal. Cholesterol fine. Letter mailed.
